To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the susceptibility of mice to infection with the coccidian parasite, E. vermiform is, depends upon the mouse strain, and that this susceptibility can be modified by immunological factors such as the production of antibody and the presence of thymic lymphocytes.

The susceptibility of mice to coccidial infection depends on the genetic background and on the strain of parasite, and that the host response is complex and may include the production of antibodies, the development of cell-mediated immunity and the activity of the complement cascade.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the host-parasite interaction in coccidiosis.
the study of the pathogenesis and immunology of the coccidial infection of mice with Eimeria vermiforis.
the development of a model for studying the mechanisms of immunity to coccidial infection and the role of different cell types in this response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the athymic mice were most susceptible to primary infection with E. verniformis and that all strains of immunologically deficient mice, with the exception of the asplenic mutants, developed immunity to reinfection with this parasite.
the strain of mice and the nature of the infection are the most important determinants of the outcome of infection.

the athymic mutants were completely susceptible to E. vermiform is and that other mice could be divided into three groups: (a) those that were resistant to primary infection and resistant to reinfection; (b) those that were susceptible to primary infection, but resistant to reinfection and (c) those that were moderately susceptible to primary infection and susceptible to reinfection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the susceptibility of the host to E. vermiform is determined by the balance between the immune response and the ability of the parasite to evade or overcome it.
the athymic mutant mice were the most susceptible and the asplenic mutants were the most resistant to coccidial infections.
the athymic mutants were the most susceptible to infection with the parasite, and that resistance to infection was associated with the presence of T cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the host response to E. vermiform is not simply a matter of the production or not of antibody but is a complex phenomenon involving many different components of the immune response, including the thymus-dependent system and the NK cells.
the mouse strain used is a key factor in determining susceptibility to infection with Eimeria vermifomis.
E. vermiformi is a good model for studying coccidiosis and the mechanisms of host resistance to this infection.
